execBuyer.headlineAccent: The answers they need to hear.
execBuyer.intro: This section is for CEOs, Managing Directors, and Commercial Directors. The ones asking: not what is this product, but what does this do to our market position.

questions.q: How do we stay relevant when our members no longer need us to exist?
questions.a: Stop competing on the value of your product. Compete on the value of your infrastructure. When your members run their business on your platform, their growth reinforces your relevance rather than eroding it. The stronger they get, the more embedded they become.
questions.emphasis: Become infrastructure. Infrastructure is not replaced. It is built around.

questions.q: How do we build a competitive position that takes years to displace?
questions.a: Platform trust is built transaction by transaction. The first organisation in a sector to own the operational layer for their members has a compounding advantage. Every month they operate the platform, the switching cost for members increases. The second organisation to do this is always a decade behind.
questions.emphasis: First mover in platform infrastructure is the strongest moat in any B2B sector.

questions.q: How do we capture value from the network we have already built?
questions.a: Right now, your members are generating thousands of transactions that are completely invisible to you. Every order, every sale, every payment is data about your sector that you do not have. A platform makes that visible — sector-wide, real-time, and commercially actionable.
questions.emphasis: Your network is generating intelligence you are not capturing. That changes.

questions.q: What does this look like in three years?
questions.a: Your members run their business on your platform. New members enter your sector and naturally onboard through you — because that is where the infrastructure is. Your commercial conversations shift from defending your position to expanding your ecosystem. Your market intelligence is deeper than any competitor can build from the outside.
questions.emphasis: In three years, the question is not why you built this. It is how you built it before anyone else.

pricing.ctaTitle: The right conversation to have first
pricing.ctaBody: Tell us your network size and sector. We will send a proposal — including what the platform would look like for your members, what your partner dashboard covers, and what the commercial structure could look like. No commitment required at this stage.

items.a: No. Powered by Pagayo is a co-brand model. Your name and identity lead. Pagayo's platform powers it. Your members experience your network's commerce platform — not Pagayo's. We are the engine. You are the face.

items.q: Do we need a tech team or IT department?
items.a: No. Configuration takes days, not months. You set your brand identity, your sector settings, and your member invitation flow. There is no development work, no system integration project, and no technical team required on your side.

items.q: What support do we need to provide to our members?
items.a: Almost none. Pagayo handles first-line support for your members directly — platform questions, technical issues, payment queries. You have a dedicated partner support line for network-level questions. Your team focuses on the commercial relationship, not the helpdesk.

items.q: Can we set our own pricing for members?
items.a: Yes. You can bundle Pagayo access as part of your existing commercial relationship, price it as a separate service, offer it as a retention benefit, or build it into a membership tier. The commercial structure between you and your members is entirely yours to design.

items.q: What happens if a member leaves our network?
items.a: They lose access to your network's platform configuration and its benefits. They can continue using Pagayo as a standard Pagayo customer — but they lose the network-specific setup, your support context, and the advantages that come from being part of your ecosystem.

items.q: How long does it take to go live?
items.a: Most networks complete configuration and activate their first cohort of members within 2–4 weeks. Larger networks with bespoke configuration requirements typically take 6–8 weeks. The member onboarding flow is five minutes per member.

items.q: Which sectors does this work for?
items.a: Any sector where your members are engaged in commerce — selling products, taking orders, managing subscriptions, or processing payments. We have experience across beauty and personal care, food and beverage, agriculture, sports and fitness, professional services, and franchise networks. If your members sell, Powered by Pagayo works.

items.q: Is this different from your Partner Programme?
items.a: Yes, fundamentally. The Partner Programme is a referral model — you earn a commission for referring businesses that pay for Pagayo themselves. Powered by Pagayo is an infrastructure model — you are the platform for your network. Different commercial logic, different relationship, different strategic value.
